***Mages of Silverquill hone the power of words. They channel the magic of light and shadow through words, whether spoken aloud, written, or signed through gestures. The words of a mage of Silverquill bring salvation to their allies and despair to their enemies.***

Source: Unearthed Arcana 79 - Mages of Strixhaven  
Classes: Bard, Warlock, or Wizard

### Using This Subclass

Upon selecting the Mage of Silverquill subclass, you gain two features: Eloquent Apprentice and Silvery Barbs.

In this subclass's features, any reference to your class refers to the class from which you gained the subclass. If you're a bard, the College of Silverquill counts as your college, if you're a warlock, the college counts as your patron, and if you're a wizard, the college counts as your tradition.

When you subsequently reach a level in your class that gives you a subclass feature, you gain one feature of your choice from the options presented here. Each feature has a class level prerequisite, as noted beneath its name. You must meet that prerequisite to gain the feature.

### Eloquent Apprentice

*Level 1+ Mage of Silverquill Feature*  
You learn one cantrip of your choice, either Sacred Flame or Vicious Mockery. It doesn't count against the number of cantrips you know, and it is added to your class spell list if it isn't there already.

Additionally, you gain proficiency in your choice of two of the following skills: Deception, Intimidation, Performance, Persuasion, or Insight.

### Silvery Barbs

*Level 1+ Mage of Silverquill Feature*

You can invoke words laced with magic to demoralize your foes and turn their misfortune into a boon to bolster your allies. Immediately after a creature you can see within 60 feet of you succeeds on an attack roll, an ability check, or a saving throw, you can use your reaction to demoralize the creature. Unless the creature is immune to being charmed, it rerolls the d20 and must use the lower roll. If the attack roll, ability check, or saving throw then fails, you can choose a different creature you can see within 60 feet of you (you can choose yourself). That creature is empowered, and can reroll one attack roll, ability check, or saving throw it makes within 1 minute and use the higher result. A creature can be empowered by only one use of this feature at a time.

Once a creature fails an attack roll, an ability check, or a saving throw because of a reroll forced by this feature, you can't use the feature again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a spell slot to use it again.

### Inky Shroud

*Level 6+ Mage of Silverquill Feature*

You learn the Darkness spell, and it is added to your class spell list if it isn't there already. If you are a wizard, you add it to your spellbook, if it's not there already.

You can cast the spell without expending a spell slot, and you can't do so again until you finish a long rest. When you cast the spell in this way, you can see normally through the darkness created, and when a creature you can see starts its turn in the darkness, you can deal 2d10 psychic damage to that creature.

You can also cast the spell normally, without the additional effects, by using spell slots you have of 2nd level or higher.

### Infusion of Eloquence

*Level 10+ Mage of Silverquill Feature*  
When you cast a spell that deals damage, you can invoke additional words of power to change the spell's damage type to your choice of psychic or radiant. Any creature damaged by the spell takes extra damage equal to your proficiency bonus and has its emotions swayed with despair or adoration, based on the damage type dealt:

**Psychic.** The creature is frightened of you until the start of your next turn.  
**Radiant.** The creature is charmed by you until the start of your next turn.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

### Word of Power

*Level 14+ Mage of Silverquill Feature*

You can invoke a word of power that is the pinnacle of your magical study. You gain the following options:

**Deadly Despair.** When the target of your Silvery Barbs fails an attack roll, an ability check, or a saving throw because of the reroll, you can invoke a word of despair to give the target vulnerability to one damage type of your choice until the start of your next turn.

**Selfless Invocation.** When a creature you can see within 60 feet of you takes damage, you can invoke a word of power using your reaction to grant the creature resistance to that damage, and you take an amount of psychic damage equal to the damage that creature takes.

name: Mage Of Witherbloom
description:
***Mages of Witherbloom draw their magic from the energy that endlessly flows from life to death, and back again. They see the duality of thriving life and inevitable death in all things, tapping and manipulating the transition of energy between these states. Some Witherbloom adherents focus on vital energies to nurture life and empower others, while others embrace the drain of vitality into decay to sap and strike down their foes.***

Source: Unearthed Arcana 79 - Mages of Strixhaven  
Classes: Druid, Warlock

### Using This Subclass

Upon selecting the Mage of Witherbloom subclass, you gain two features: Witherbloom Spells and Essence Tap.

In this subclass's features, any reference to your class refers to the class from which you gained the subclass. If you're a druid, the College of Witherbloom counts as your circle, and if you're a warlock, the college counts as your patron.

When you subsequently reach a level in your class that gives you a subclass feature, you gain one feature of your choice from the options presented here. Each feature has a class level prerequisite, as noted beneath its name. You must meet that prerequisite to gain the feature.

### Witherbloom Spells

*Level 1+ Mage of Witherbloom Feature*

You learn the cantrip Spare the Dying and the 1st level spells Cure Wounds and Inflict Wounds. You learn additional spells when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown on the Witherbloom Spells table.

Each of these spells count as a class spell for you, but it doesn't count against the number of spells you know. If you are a druid, you always have the spells prepared, and they don't count against the number of spells you can prepare each day.

##### Witherbloom Spells

| Class Level | Spells |
|---|---|
| 3rd | Lesser Restoration, Ray of Enfeeblement |
| 5th | Revivify, Vampiric Touch |
| 7th | Blight, Greater Restoration |
| 9th | Antilife Shell, Mass Cure Wounds |

### Essence Tap

*Level 1+ Mage of Witherbloom Feature*

As a bonus action, you can draw on a reservoir of life essence to empower yourself for 1 minute, or until you use this feature again. For the duration, you gain one of the following benefits of your choice:

**Overgrowth.** When you choose this benefit, and as a bonus action on subsequent turns while the benefit lasts, you can expend and roll one Hit Die. You regain a number of hit points equal to the number rolled plus your spellcasting ability modifier.

**Withering Strike.** When you deal damage, you can change the damage type to necrotic, and you ignore resistance to necrotic damage.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

### Witherbloom Brew

*Level 6+ Mage of Witherbloom Feature*  
You gain proficiency with herbalism kits if you don't already have it.

When you finish a long rest, you can use an herbalism kit and a pot or cauldron to create magical brews. You create a number of brews equal to your proficiency bonus. Each brew requires its own flask. A brew retains its magical potency for 24 hours or until it is used. For each brew, choose one of the following effects:

**Fortifying.** When you create this brew, choose a damage type from the following list: cold, fire, necrotic, poison, or radiant. A creature can drink this brew or administer it to another creature as an action. The recipient gains resistance to the chosen damage type for 1 hour.

**Quickening.** A creature can drink this brew or administer it to another creature as an action. The recipient regains 2d6 hit points, and one disease or condition from the following list affecting the recipient ends (brew user's choice): charmed, frightened, paralyzed, poisoned, stunned.

**Toxifying.** As an action, a creature can apply this brew to a simple or martial weapon. The next time the weapon or a piece of ammunition fired by it hits a creature within 1 hour, the target takes 2d6 poison damage and must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC or be poisoned for 1 minute.

### Witherbloom Adept

*Level 10+ Mage of Witherbloom Feature*  
Your connection to the flow of life force deepens. Once per turn when you deal necrotic damage or restore hit points using a spell, one target of the spell takes additional damage or regains additional hit points equal to your proficiency bonus.

### Withering Vortex

*Level 14+ Mage of Witherbloom Feature*  
When you cast a spell using a spell slot that deals necrotic damage to any number of creatures that aren't Undead or Constructs, choose one of the creatures that took damage. You drain an amount of life energy equal to half the damage dealt to the chosen creature. One creature other than yourself that you can see within 30 feet of you regains a number of hit points equal to the life energy drained.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

name: Quick Characters
description:
Sometimes you need quick characters for a D&D session. Whether you're running an impromptu game with limited time for character creation, you want to get a new player into an established game quickly, or you need a new PC to replace a dead adventurer, these optional rules are for you. These rules can be used instead of the normal process of character creation, replacing the choice and creativity of that process with a series of tables that quickly generate a 1st-level character.

With the exception of backgrounds, these rules focus on the character options available in the D&D Basic Rules as a means of keeping things simple.

|  |
|---|

## Alignment

Roll a d6 to determine your character's alignment.

| d6 | Alignment |
|---|---|
| 1 | Lawful Good |
| 2 | Neutral Good |
| 3 | Chaotic Good |
| 4 | Lawful Neutral |
| 5 | Neutral |
| 6 | Chaotic Neutral |

In place of a background feature, once during any game session, you can pick a nonplayer character you meet and declare that your character knows that NPC. The relationship is respectful but not necessarily friendly. The DM determines the exact nature of your relationship.

## Class and Abilities

Roll a d6 to determine your class from the following table, which is more likely to generate a fighter or cleric than a rogue or wizard. Especially if you're randomly generating an entire party, tilting the odds in favor of fighters and clerics can help shore up a group's ability to survive in combat. Alternatively (or if you're generating a single character joining an already balanced party), you can roll a d4 and give each class an equal chance of being generated.

| d6 | d4 | Class |
|---|---|---|
| 1-2 | 1 | Cleric |
| 3-4 | 2 | Fighter |
| 5 | 3 | Rogue |
| 6 | 4 | Wizard |

When determining your ability scores, your choice of class shapes which abilities are of most use to your character. Roll a d6 to determine the ability score array your character uses. Then assign those numbers to your abilities in an order determined by your class.

| d6 | Score Array |
|---|---|
| 1 | 18, 14, 12, 8, 8, 6 |
| 2 | 16, 14, 14, 10, 10, 8 |
| 3 | 16, 16, 12, 10, 8, 8 |
| 4 | 16, 12, 12, 12, 10, 8 |
| 5 | 14, 14, 12, 12, 12, 12 |
| 6 | 14, 14, 14, 12, 12, 10 |

**Cleric.** Wisdom, Strength, Constitution, Charisma, Dexterity, Intelligence.  
**Fighter.** Strength, Constitution, Dexterity, Wisdom, Intelligence, Charisma.  
**Rogue.** Dexterity, Charisma, Intelligence, Constitution, Strength, Wisdom.  
**Wizard.** Intelligence, Dexterity, Wisdom, Charisma, Constitution, Strength.

For example, a player creating a cleric rolls a 4 for the character's ability score array—16, 12, 12, 12, 10, and 8. Those numbers are assigned in that order to the ability scores listed for clerics, yielding a character with Strength 12, Dexterity 10, Constitution 12, Intelligence 8, Wisdom 16, and Charisma 12.

After you assign your character's ability scores, but before applying any modifiers for your race (see  
below), you can swap any two scores.

### Equipment

Your class also determines your equipment. Select gear from your class's quick equipment choices, except for any of the prebuilt packs such as the explorer's pack or the priest's pack (see below).

Alternatively, you can select one of the following default equipment packages:

- **Cleric:** Mace, scale mail, light crossbow and 20 bolts, shield, holy symbol
- **Fighter:** Chain mail, longsword, shield, light crossbow and 20 bolts
- **Rogue:** Shortsword, shortbow and 20 arrows, leather armor, two daggers, thieves' tools
- **Wizard:** Dagger, component pouch, spellbook

Then select one of the following standard equipment packs for your character:

- Backpack, sack, lantern, 2 oil flasks, tinderbox, 12 pitons, hammer, waterskin, rations (4 days), 5 gp
- Backpack, 2 sacks, 6 torches, 3 oil flasks, tinderbox, 10-foot pole, 50 feet of rope, waterskin, rations (4 days), steel mirror
- Backpack, 4 sacks, holy symbol or thieves' tools, 12 pitons, 50 feet of rope, waterskin, rations (4

days)

All characters also gain a dagger and either a light crossbow and 10 bolts, or a set of 5 javelins.

description:

**The Ranger (Ambuscade)**

# Class Features

As a ranger, you gain the following class features.

##### Hit Points

**Hit Dice:** 2d6 per ranger level  
**Hit Points at 1st Level:** 12 + your Constitution modifier  
**Hit Points at Higher Levels:** 2d6 (or 7) + your Constitution modifier per ranger level after 1st

##### Proficiencies

**Armor:** Light armor, shields  
**Weapons:** Simple weapons, martial weapons  
**Tools:** Herbalism kit  
**Saving Throws:** Dexterity, Wisdom  
**Skills:** Choose three from Animal Handling, Athletics, Insight, Investigation, Nature, Perception, Stealth, and Survival

##### Equipment

You start with the following equipment, in addition to the equipment granted by your background:

- Leather armor
- (a) two shortswords or (b) two martial melee weapons or (c) a martial weapon and a shield
- (a) a dungeoneer's pack or (b) an explorer's pack
- A longbow and a quiver of 20 arrows or (b) a martial weapon

### Ambuscade

Rangers strike first and strike hard. When you roll initiative, you gain a special turn that takes place before other creatures can act. On this turn, you can use your action to take either the Attack or Hide action.

If more than one creature in an encounter has this feature, they all act first in order of initiative, then the regular initiative order begins.

If you would normally be surprised at the start of an encounter, you are not surprised but you do not gain this extra turn.

### Natural Explorer

Also at 1st level, you are particularly familiar with one type of natural environment and are adept at traveling and surviving in such regions. Choose one type of favored terrain: arctic, coast, desert, forest, grassland, mountain, swamp, or the Underdark. When you make an Intelligence or Wisdom check related to your favored terrain, your proficiency bonus is doubled if you are using a skill that you're proficient in.

While traveling for an hour or more in your favored terrain, you gain the following benefits:

- Difficult terrain doesn't slow your group's travel.
- Your group can't become lost except by magical means.
- Even when you are engaged in another activity while traveling (such as foraging, navigating, or tracking), you remain alert to danger.
- If you are traveling alone, you can move stealthily at a normal pace.
- When you forage, you find twice as much food as you normally would.
- While tracking other creatures, you also learn their exact number, their sizes, and how long ago they passed through the area.

### Fighting Style

At 2nd level, you adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one of the following options. You can't take a Fighting Style option more than once, even if you later get to choose again.

- **Archery.** You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls you make with ranged weapons.

- **Blind Fighting.** You have blind sight with a range of 10 feet. Within that range, you can effectively see anything that isn't behind total cover, even if you're blinded or in darkness. Moreover, you can see an invisible creature within that range, unless the creature successfully hides from you.

- **Defense.** While you are wearing armor, you gain a +1 bonus to AC.

- **Druidic Warrior.** You learn two cantrips of your choice from the Druid spell list. They count as ranger spells for you, and Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for them. Whenever you gain a level in this class, you can replace one of these cantrips with another cantrip from the Druid spell list.

- **Dueling.** When you are wielding a melee weapon in one hand and no other weapons, you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls with that weapon.

- **Thrown Weapon Fighting.** You can draw a weapon that has the thrown property as part of the attack you make with the weapon.
  - In addition, when you hit with a ranged attack using a thrown weapon, you gain a +2 bonus to the damage roll.

- **Two-Weapon Fighting.** When you engage in two-weapon fighting, you can add your ability modifier to the damage of the second attack.

- **Close Quarters Shooter (UA).** When making a ranged attack while you are within 5 feet of a hostile creature, you do not have disadvantage on the attack roll. Your ranged attacks ignore half cover and three-quarters cover against targets within 30 feet of you. You have a +1 bonus to attack rolls on ranged attacks.

- **Interception (UA).** When a creature you can see hits a target that is within 5 feet of you with an attack, you can use your reaction to reduce the damage the target takes by 1d10 + your proficiency bonus (to a minimum of 0 damage). You must be wielding a shield or a simple or martial weapon to use this reaction.

- **Mariner (UA).** As long as you are not wearing heavy armor or using a shield, you have a swimming speed and a climbing speed equal to your normal speed, and you gain a +1 bonus to armor class.

- **Tunnel Fighter (UA).** As a bonus action, you can enter a defensive stance that lasts until the start of your next turn. While in your defensive stance, you can make opportunity attacks without using your reaction, and you can use your reaction to make a melee attack against a creature that moves more than 5 feet while within your reach.

- **Unarmed Fighting (UA).** Your unarmed strikes can deal bludgeoning damage equal to 1d6 + your Strength modifier. If you strike with two free hands, the d6 becomes a d8.
  - When you successfully start a grapple, you can deal 1d4 bludgeoning damage to the grappled creature. Until the grapple ends, you can also deal this damage to the creature whenever you hit it with a melee attack.

### Skirmisher's Stealth

Beginning at 2nd level, you combine speed and stealth in combat to make yourself hard to pin down. You are difficult to detect even if you attack or otherwise take actions that would normally reveal your presence.

At the start of your turn, pick a creature you are hidden from. You remain hidden from that creature during your turn, regardless of your actions or the actions of other creatures. As a bonus action at the end of your turn, you can make a Dexterity (Stealth) check to hide again if you fulfil the conditions needed to hide. Otherwise, creatures are aware of you at the end of your turn.

### Spirit Path

At 3rd level, you form a bond with a nature spirit — a companion forged by your link to the wild. This spirit companion protects you as you travel and watches your back in battle. You choose a ranger path that shapes your spirit companion and its magic: the Guardian, the Seeker, or the Stalker.

| Ranger Paths |
|---|
| Guardian |
| Seeker |
| Stalker |

#### Spirit Companion

All rangers gain a spirit companion and the ability to invoke its magical power. (Your spirit companion grants you one benefit you can call on in this playtest version of the revised ranger, with more benefits gained at higher levels.) You regain your ability to call on your spirit companion in this way when you finish a short or long rest.

Once per day as a bonus action, you can command your spirit companion to materialize as a living creature, determined by the ranger path you choose. Your spirit companion manifests as an animal for 1 minute or until your concentration is broken (as if you are concentrating on a spell). You can also dismiss it as a bonus action.

The manifested creature gains a bonus to attack rolls and saving throws equal to your Wisdom modifier. It uses the hit points in the animal's stat block or half your hit point maximum, whichever is higher.

The manifested creature takes its turn on your initiative and acts immediately after you. You control its actions, even if you are unconscious or otherwise unable to act.

### Ability Score Improvement

When you reach 4th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

### Extra Attack

Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

*See Also: Official Published Ranger Class*

# Class Features

As a ranger, you gain the following class features.

##### Hit Points

**Hit Dice:** 1d10 per ranger level  
**Hit Points at 1st Level:** 10 + your Constitution modifier  
**Hit Points at Higher Levels:** 1d10 (or 6) + your Constitution modifier per ranger level after 1st

##### Proficiencies

**Armor:** Light armor, medium armor, shields  
**Weapons:** Simple weapons, martial weapons  
**Tools:** None  
**Saving Throws:** Strength, Dexterity  
**Skills:** Choose three from Animal Handling, Athletics, Insight, Investigation, Nature, Perception, Stealth, and Survival

##### Equipment

You start with the following equipment, in addition to the equipment granted by your background:

- (a) scale mail or (b) leather armor
- (a) two shortswords or (b) two simple melee weapons
- (a) a dungeoneer's pack or (b) an explorer's pack
- A longbow and a quiver of 20 arrows

### Favored Enemy

Beginning at 1st level, you have significant experience studying, tracking, hunting, and even talking to a certain type of enemy.

Choose a type of favored enemy: aberrations, beasts, celestials, constructs, dragons, elementals, fey, fiends, giants, monstrosities, oozes, plants, or undead. Alternatively, you can select two races of humanoid (such as gnolls and orcs) as favored enemies.

You have advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks to track your favored enemies, as well as on Intelligence checks to recall information about them.

When you gain this feature, you also learn one language of your choice that is spoken by your favored enemies, if they speak one at all.

You choose one additional favored enemy, as well as an associated language, at 6th and 14th level. As you gain levels, your choices should reflect the types of monsters you have encountered on your adventures.

### Favored Foe (Optional)

This 1st-level feature replaces the Favored Enemy feature and works with the Foe Slayer feature. You gain no benefit from the replaced feature and don't qualify for anything in the game that requires it.

When you hit a creature with an attack roll, you can call on your mystical bond with nature to mark the target as your favored enemy for 1 minute or until you lose your concentration (as if you were concentrating on a spell).

The first time on each of your turns that you hit the favored enemy and deal damage to it, including when you mark it, you increase that damage by 1d4.

You can use this feature to mark a favored enemy a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

This feature's extra damage increases when you reach certain levels in this class: to 1d6 at 6th level and to 1d8 at 14th level.

### Natural Explorer

Also at 1st level, you are particularly familiar with one type of natural environment and are adept at traveling and surviving in such regions. Choose one type of favored terrain: arctic, coast, desert, forest, grassland, mountain, swamp, or the Underdark. When you make an Intelligence or Wisdom check related to your favored terrain, your proficiency bonus is doubled if you are using a skill that you're proficient in.

While traveling for an hour or more in your favored terrain, you gain the following benefits:

- Difficult terrain doesn't slow your group's travel.
- Your group can't become lost except by magical means.
- Even when you are engaged in another activity while traveling (such as foraging, navigating, or tracking), you remain alert to danger.
- If you are traveling alone, you can move stealthily at a normal pace.
- When you forage, you find twice as much food as you normally would.
- While tracking other creatures, you also learn their exact number, their sizes, and how long ago they passed through the area.

You choose additional favored terrain types at 6th and 10th level.

### Deft Explorer (Optional)

This 1st-level feature replaces the Natural Explorer feature. You gain no benefit from the replaced feature and don't qualify for anything in the game that requires it.

You are an unsurpassed explorer and survivor, both in the wilderness and in dealing with others on your travels. You gain the Canny benefit below, and you gain an additional benefit when you reach 6th level and 10th level in this class.

###### Canny (1st Level)

Choose one of your skill proficiencies. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make using the chosen skill.

You can also speak, read, and write 2 additional languages of your choice.

###### Roving (6th Level)

Your walking speed increases by 5, and you gain a climbing speed and a swimming speed equal to your walking speed.

###### Tireless (10th Level)

As an action, you can give yourself a number of temporary hit points equal to 1d8 + your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1 temporary hit point). You can use this action a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

In addition, whenever you finish a short rest, your exhaustion level, if any, is decreased by 1.

- **Close Quarters Shooter (UA).** When making a ranged attack while you are within 5 feet of a hostile creature, you do not have disadvantage on the attack roll. - **Unarmed Fighting (UA).** Your unarmed strikes can deal bludgeoning damage equal to 1d6 + your Strength modifier. If you strike with two free hands, the d6 becomes a d8.
  - When you successfully start a grapple, you can deal 1d4 bludgeoning damage to the grappled creature. Until the grapple ends, you can also deal this damage to the creature whenever you hit it with a melee attack.

### Combat Superiority

At 2nd level, you learn maneuvers that are fueled by special dice called superiority dice.  
Maneuvers. You learn two maneuvers of your choice, which are chosen from the list of maneuvers available to fighters with the Battle Master archetype. Many maneuvers enhance an attack in some way. You can use only one maneuver per attack.

You learn one additional maneuver of your choice at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th levels. Each time you learn a new maneuver, you can also replace one maneuver you know with a different one.

**Superiority Dice.** You have four superiority dice, which are d8s. A superiority die is expended when you use it. You regain all of your expended superiority dice when you finish a short or long rest.

You gain another superiority die at 9th level and one more at 17th level.

**Saving Throws.** Some of your maneuvers require your target to make a saving throw to resist the maneuver's effects. The saving throw DC is calculated as follows:

**Maneuver save DC** = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice)

### Poultices

At 3rd level, you can create special herbal poultices that have healing power comparable to some potions. You can spend 1 hour gathering herbs and preparing herbal poultices using treated bandages to create a number of such poultices equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum 1). You can carry a number of poultices at one time equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum 1). The poultices you create cannot be applied by anyone but you. After 24 hours, any poultices that you have not used lose their potency.

If you spend 1 minute applying one of your poultices to a wounded humanoid creature, thereby expending its use, that creature regains 1d6 hit points for every two ranger levels you have (rounded up).

### Ranger Conclave

At 3rd level, you choose to emulate the ideals and training of a ranger conclave. Your choice grants you features at 3rd level and again at 7th, 11th, and 15th level.

| Conclave | Source |
|---|---|
| Beast Master | Player's Handbook |
| Hunter | Player's Handbook |

### Ability Score Improvement

When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

### Martial Versatility (Optional)

Whenever you reach a level in this class that grants the Ability Score Improvement feature, you can replace a fighting style you know with another fighting style available to rangers. This replacement represents a shift of focus in your martial practice.

### Extra Attack

Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

### Fleet of Foot

Starting at 8th level, moving through nonmagical difficult terrain costs you no extra movement. You can also pass through nonmagical plants without being slowed by them and without taking damage from them if they have thorns, spines, or a similar hazard.

In addition, you have advantage on saving throws against plants that are magically created or manipulated to impede movement, such those created by the Entangle spell.

### Natural Antivenom

Starting at 9th level, you have advantage on saving throws against poison and have resistance to poison damage. Additionally, you can use one of your poultices to cure one poison effect on the creature you are applying it to, in addition to restoring hit points.

### Hide in Plain Sight

Starting at 10th level, you can spend 1 minute creating camouflage for yourself. You must have access to fresh mud, dirt, plants, soot, and other naturally occurring materials with which to create your camouflage.

Once you are camouflaged in this way, you can try to hide by pressing yourself up against a solid surface, such as a tree or wall, that is at least as tall and wide as you are. You gain a +10 bonus to Dexterity (Stealth) checks as long as you remain there without moving or taking actions. Once you move or take an action or a reaction, you must camouflage yourself again to gain this benefit.

### Nature's Veil (Optional)

This 10th-level feature replaces the Hide in Plain Sight feature. You gain no benefit from the replaced feature and don't qualify for anything in the game that requires it.

You draw on the powers of nature to hide yourself from view briefly. As a bonus action, you can magically become invisible, along with any equipment you are wearing or carrying, until the start of your next turn.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

### Call Natural Allies

Starting at 13th level, when you are in an area of your favored terrain, you can call natural creatures from that terrain to fight on your behalf, using your attunement to the natural world to convince them to aid you. The DM chooses beasts appropriate to the terrain to come to your aid from among those that could hear you and that are within 1 mile of you, in one of the following groups:

- One beast of challenge rating 2 or lower
- Two beasts of challenge rating 1 or lower
- Four beasts of challenge rating 1/2 or lower
- Eight beasts of challenge rating 1/4 or lower

These beasts approach you from their current location, and will fight alongside you, attacking any creatures that are hostile to you. They are friendly to you and your comrades, and you roll initiative for the called creatures as a group, which takes its own turns. The DM has the creatures' statistics.

After 1 hour, these beasts return to their previous location. Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again in the same general area for 24 hours, since the same animals will not repeatedly heed your call.

### Vanish

Starting at 14th level, you can use the Hide action as a bonus action on your turn. Also, you can't be tracked by nonmagical means, unless you choose to leave a trail.

### Relentless

Starting at 17th level, when you roll initiative and have no superiority dice remaining, you regain 1 superiority die.

### Feral Senses

At 18th level, you gain preternatural senses that help you fight creatures you can't see. When you attack a creature you can't see, your inability to see it doesn't impose disadvantage on your attack rolls against it.

You are also aware of the location of any invisible creature within 30 feet of you, provided that the creature isn't hidden from you and you aren't blinded or deafened.

### Foe Slayer

At 20th level, you become an unparalleled hunter of your enemies. Once on each of your turns, you can add your Wisdom modifier to the attack roll or the damage roll of an attack you make against one of your favored enemies. You can choose to use this feature before or after the roll, but before any effects of the roll are applied.

name: Ranger, Revised
description:
***Far from the bustle of cities and towns, past the hedges that shelter the most distant farms from the terrors of the wild, amid the dense-packed trees of trackless forests and across wide and empty plains, rangers keep their unending watch.***

*You must have a Dexterity score and a Wisdom score of 13 or higher in order to multiclass in or out of this class.*

# Class Features

As a ranger, you gain the following class features.

##### Hit Points

**Hit Dice:** 1d10 per ranger level  
**Hit Points at 1st Level:** 10 + your Constitution modifier  
**Hit Points at Higher Levels:** 1d10 (or 6) + your Constitution modifier per ranger level after 1st

##### Proficiencies

**Armor:** Light armor, medium armor, shields  
**Weapons:** Simple weapons, martial weapons  
**Tools:** None  
**Saving Throws:** Strength, Dexterity  
**Skills:** Choose three from Animal Handling, Athletics, Insight, Investigation, Nature, Perception, Stealth, and Survival

##### Equipment

You start with the following equipment, in addition to the equipment granted by your background:

- (a) scale mail or (b) leather armor
- (a) two shortswords or (b) two simple melee weapons
- (a) a dungeoneer's pack or (b) an explorer's pack
- A longbow and a quiver of 20 arrows

### Favored Enemy

Beginning at 1st level, you have significant experience studying, tracking, hunting, and even talking to a certain type of enemy commonly encountered in the wilds.

Choose a type of favored enemy: beasts, fey, humanoids, monstrosities, or undead. You gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls with weapon attacks against creatures of the chosen type. Additionally, you have advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks to track your favored enemies, as well as on Intelligence checks to recall information about them.

When you gain this feature, you also learn one language of your choice, typically one spoken by your favored enemy or creatures associated with it. However, you are free to pick any language you wish to learn.

### Natural Explorer

You are a master of navigating the natural world, and you react with swift and decisive action when attacked. This grants you the following benefits:

- You ignore difficult terrain.

- You have advantage on initiative rolls.

- On your first turn during combat, you have advantage on attack rolls against creatures that have not yet acted.

In addition, you are skilled at navigating the wilderness. You gain the following benefits when traveling for an hour or more:

- Difficult terrain doesn't slow your group's travel.

- Your group can't become lost except by magical means.

- Even when you are engaged in another activity while traveling (such as foraging, navigating, or tracking), you remain alert to danger.

- If you are traveling alone, you can move stealthily at a normal pace.

- When you forage, you find twice as much food as you normally would.

- While tracking other creatures, you also learn their exact number, their sizes, and how long ago they passed through the area.

### Fighting Style

At 2nd level, you adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one of the following options. You can't take a Fighting Style option more than once, even if you later get to choose again.

- **Archery.** You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls you make with ranged weapons.

- **Close Quarters Shooter (UA).** When making a ranged attack while you are within 5 feet of a hostile creature, you do not have disadvantage on the attack roll. Your ranged attacks ignore half cover and three-quarters cover against targets within 30 feet of you. You have a +1 bonus to attack rolls on ranged attacks.

- **Defense.** While you are wearing armor, you gain a +1 bonus to AC.

- **Dueling.** When you are wielding a melee weapon in one hand and no other weapons, you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls with that weapon.

- **Mariner (UA).** As long as you are not wearing heavy armor or using a shield, you have a swimming speed and a climbing speed equal to your normal speed, and you gain a +1 bonus to armor class.

- **Tunnel Fighter (UA).** As a bonus action, you can enter a defensive stance that lasts until the start of your next turn. While in your defensive stance, you can make opportunity attacks without using your reaction, and you can use your reaction to make a melee attack against a creature that moves more than 5 feet while within your reach.

- **Two-Weapon Fighting.** When you engage in two-weapon fighting, you can add your ability modifier to the damage of the second attack.

- **Druidic Warrior (UA).** You learn two cantrips of your choice from the druid spell list. They count as ranger spells for you, and Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for them. Whenever you gain a level in this class, you can replace one of these cantrips with another cantrip from the druid spell list.

- **Blind Fighting (UA).** Being unable to see a creature doesn't impose disadvantage on your attack rolls against it, provided the creature isn't hidden from you.

- **Interception (UA).** When a creature you can see hits a target that is within 5 feet of you with an attack, you can use your reaction to reduce the damage the target takes by 1d10 + your proficiency bonus (to a minimum of 0 damage). You must be wielding a shield or a simple or martial weapon to use this reaction.

- **Thrown Weapon Fighting (UA).** You can draw a weapon that has the thrown property as part of the attack you make with the weapon.
  - In addition, when you hit with a ranged attack using a thrown weapon, you gain a +2 bonus to the damage roll.

- **Unarmed Fighting (UA).** Your unarmed strikes can deal bludgeoning damage equal to 1d6 + your Strength modifier. If you strike with two free hands, the d6 becomes a d8.
  - When you successfully start a grapple, you can deal 1d4 bludgeoning damage to the grappled creature. Until the grapple ends, you can also deal this damage to the creature whenever you hit it with a melee attack.

### Spellcasting

By the time you reach 2nd level, you have learned to use the magical essence of nature to cast spells, much as a druid does.

###### Spell Slots

The Ranger table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your spells of 1st level and higher. To cast one of these spells, you must expend a slot of the spell's level or higher. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a long rest.

For example, if you know the 1st-level spell Animal Friendship and have a 1st-level and a 2nd-level spell slot available, you can cast Animal Friendship using either slot.

###### Spells Known of 1st Level and Higher

You know two 1st-level spells of your choice from the ranger spell list.  
The Spells Known column of the Ranger table shows when you learn more ranger spells of your choice. Each of these spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For instance, when you reach 5th level in this class, you can learn one new spell of 1st or 2nd level.

Additionally, when you gain a level in this class, you can choose one of the ranger spells you know and replace it with another spell from the ranger spell list, which also must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

###### Spellcasting Ability

Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your ranger spells, since your magic draws on your attunement to nature. You use your Wisdom whenever a spell refers to your spellcasting ability. In addition, you use your Wisdom modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a ranger spell you cast and when making an attack roll with one.

**Spell save DC** = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier

**Spell attack modifier** = your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier

### Primeval Awareness

Beginning at 3rd level, your mastery of ranger lore allows you to establish a powerful link to beasts and to the land around you.

You have an innate ability to communicate with beasts, and they recognize you as a kindred spirit. Through sounds and gestures, you can communicate simple ideas to a beast as an action, and can read its basic mood and intent. You learn its emotional state, whether it is affected by magic of any sort, its short-term needs (such as food or safety), and actions you can take (if any) to persuade it to not attack.

You cannot use this ability against a creature that you have attacked within the past 10 minutes.

Additionally, you can attune your senses to determine if any of your favored enemies lurk nearby. By spending 1 uninterrupted minute in concentration (as if you were concentrating on a spell), you can sense whether any of your favored enemies are present within 5 miles of you. This feature reveals which of your favored enemies are present, their numbers, and the creatures' general direction and distance (in miles) from you.

If there are multiple groups of your favored enemies within range, you learn this information for each group.

### Ranger Conclave

At 3rd level, you choose to emulate the ideals and training of a ranger conclave. Your choice grants you features at 3rd level and again at 7th, 11th, and 15th level.

| Conclave | Source |
|---|---|
| Beast | Unearthed Arcana 17 - The Ranger, Revised |
| Deep Stalker | Unearthed Arcana 17 - The Ranger, Revised |
| Hunter | Unearthed Arcana 17 - The Ranger, Revised |
| Monster Slayer | Unearthed Arcana 35 - A Trio of Subclasses |

### Ability Score Improvement

When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

### Greater Favored Enemy

At 6th level, you are ready to hunt even deadlier game. Choose a type of greater favored enemy: aberrations, celestials, constructs, dragons, elementals, fiends, or giants. You gain all the benefits against this chosen enemy that you normally gain against your favored enemy, including an additional language. Your bonus to damage rolls against all your favored enemies increases to +4.

Additionally, you have advantage on saving throws against the spells and abilities used by a greater favored enemy.

### Fleet of Foot

Beginning at 8th level, you can use the Dash action as a bonus action on your turn.

### Hide in Plain Sight

Starting at 10th level, you can remain perfectly still for long periods of time to set up ambushes.

When you attempt to hide on your turn, you can opt to not move on that turn. If you avoid moving, creatures that attempt to detect you take a −10 penalty to their Wisdom (Perception) checks until the start of your next turn. You lose this benefit if you move or fall prone, either voluntarily or because of some external effect. You are still automatically detected if any effect or action causes you to no longer be hidden.

If you are still hidden on your next turn, you can continue to remain motionless and gain this benefit until you are detected.

### Vanish

Starting at 14th level, you can use the Hide action as a bonus action on your turn. Also, you can't be tracked by nonmagical means, unless you choose to leave a trail.

### Feral Senses

At 18th level, you gain preternatural senses that help you fight creatures you can't see. When you attack a creature you can't see, your inability to see it doesn't impose disadvantage on your attack rolls against it.

You are also aware of the location of any invisible creature within 30 feet of you, provided that the creature isn't hidden from you and you aren't blinded or deafened.

### Foe Slayer

At 20th level, you become an unparalleled hunter of your enemies. Once on each of your turns, you can add your Wisdom modifier to the attack roll or the damage roll of an attack you make. You can choose to use this feature before or after the roll, but before any effects of the roll are applied.

*See also: official ranger class*

name: Bejeweled Conclave
description:
The Bejeweled Conclave is known as an organization of professional entertainers and mediators who cater to wealthy clients. They host glamorous parties, serve as courtiers, broker deals, and provide entertainment for exclusive functions.

But the Bejeweled Conclave wields far more influence than its publicly known services indicate. Consummate agents behind the throne, the enchanters of the Bejeweled Conclave cultivate elite connections and shift the balance of power in cities across the world.

# Goals and Activities

The Bejeweled Conclave seeks to increase its sway across the multiverse. The faction engages skilled diplomats, courtiers, and entertainers and hones their abilities. Enchanters and spies receive a more clandestine, but no less thorough, education. The conclave prizes subtlety and secrecy above all; members are taught that it's better to fail a mission and keep the conclave's secrets than to succeed at the cost of exposing the faction's true goals.

The Bejeweled Conclave operates in major cities throughout the multiverse. Distance keeps members from knowing all their peers, but the faction is quick to celebrate successes, building loyalty and camaraderie within its ranks. While all members learn conversational tricks to offer convincing praise, the compliments members bestow on each other are usually genuine.

Conclave members understand that overtly using Enchantment magic risks exposing them as more than entertainers and courtiers. If a member must modify a noble's memories or magically dominate a general, they undertake significant planning to conceal their involvement.

# Leadership and Organization

More experienced members of the Bejeweled Conclave oversee operations assigned to junior members. Valuable secrets are reported through this hierarchy up to the faction's highest ranks, referred to as the Whisper Network. These leaders hoard a treasure trove of secrets; there are few facts about the movers and shakers of civilization that the Bejeweled Conclave doesn't know.

Conclave members are trusted to act alone when necessary, such as when an important client insists on hiring only a single mediator or companion. When possible, though, senior members politely request that their "junior clerks" or "associates in training" handle more workaday aspects of their affairs. Such requests, which might include subtle magical compulsion, are a ruse to bring another trained member to operate from the shadows. As a result, clients who planned to hire only one member of the Bejeweled Conclave often find themselves engaging two or three.

## Whisper Network

Members of the Whisper Network keep their identities private, even from their peers. The only exception is Madame Hestia Ilverne (Medium Noble Prodigy), a courteous human Whisper Network member who heads the conclave's public-facing efforts. Rumors within the faction claim that Madame Ilverne is among the lowest ranked of the leaders, but she seems nothing but pleased with her position.

Whether members of the Whisper Network work as music instructors, clerks, dancers, or cooks, they keep an eye on all aspects of Bejeweled Conclave activities. If they have edicts or missions to impart, they do so through Madame Ilverne. When she casually mentions a task to a member with the words "The Network would prefer a favor," all comprehend the seriousness of the request.

## Lurewood Mansion

A regal manor house in the garden district of a major city, Lurewood Mansion is the conclave's academy. The previous owners donated their property generations ago for unknown reasons. The manor's architecture has been adapted to include numerous salons and studies, as well as a fine kitchen.

In the studies, members of the Bejeweled Conclave learn to negotiate deals and defuse arguments. In the salons, singers, dancers, and musicians practice entertainment suitable for elevated private parties, from subdued chamber music to sensual dances to heart-wrenching ballads. New faction members take lessons here no matter how polished they are when recruited, if for no other reason than to bolster the illusion that negotiation and entertainment are the Bejeweled Conclave's prime objectives.

Beneath the mansion, a dizzying maze of chambers connected through locked doors and one-way mirrors facilitates practice in eavesdropping, lock-picking, quick changes, and stealthy escapes. Other rooms allow members to rest out of sight. The heart of the maze contains the mansion's best-kept secret: workrooms where enchanters teach apprentice mages the arts of twisting minds, magically hiding secrets, and erasing memories.

## Joining the Conclave

Aspiring faction members can't join the Bejeweled Conclave by requesting admission; members inevitably deny that there are any openings in what they claim is simply a loose professional organization.

Entry is only by invitation. Senior members carefully watch entertainers and mediators who have impressive public reputations. Those who seem particularly shrewd and ambitious might receive an invitation for free training in their specialties at Lurewood Mansion, hosted by Madame Ilverne.

Once an invitee arrives, Madame Ilverne engages them in cryptic conversation. If the potential member impresses her with their poise, acumen, and discretion, she invites them to join the faction. Otherwise, she thanks them for their time and sends them on their way without ever indicating that the mansion is anything other than a professional academy.

# Renown Rewards

Characters gain renown with the Bejeweled Conclave by sharing valuable secrets or completing conclave missions. As their Renown Scores increase, they gain access to various perks, as shown on the Bejeweled Conclave Renown table. If your campaign doesn't use renown, the DM decides if and when characters earn these perks.

**Bejeweled Conclave Renown**

| Renown Score | Reward |
|---|---|
| 3+ | You can consult the Bejeweled Conclave before meeting a significant figure for the first time to learn a personal secret—humorous, embarrassing, or otherwise socially relevant—about that person. |
| 5+ | You can stay in Lurewood Mansion or any other residence operated by the conclave, providing you a Modest lifestyle for free. If you have just returned from a dangerous locale, conclave members insist you first take a bath. |
| 10 | The first time your Renown Score reaches 10, the Bejeweled Conclave gives you one Uncommon magic item—usually a Ring or a Wondrous Item. |
| 15+ | Your lifestyle at Lurewood Manor or any conclave residence increases to Comfortable. Additionally, you can request the aid of 1d4 Spies for a mission. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases. |
| 20+ | If you are arrested for anything short of treason in any land where the Bejeweled Conclave operates, the conclave finds a way to have your charges dismissed. |
| 25 | You can arrange for a meeting with Madame Hestia Ilverne. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases. |
| 30 | The first time your Renown Score reaches 30, the conclave teaches you its entrancing magic. You always have the Enthrall spell prepared, and you can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a Long Rest. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell (choose when you gain this reward). You can also cast this spell using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level. |
| 40+ | At your instruction, one of the conclave members casts Modify Memory (save DC 15) for free on a target of your choice. You must have met or seen the target at least once within the last 30 days, and the spell is cast within 24 hours of you choosing your target. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases. |
| 50+ | Members of the conclave openly share information with you. Additionally, the first time your Renown Score reaches 50, the Bejeweled Conclave imparts a significant secret about you that you didn't know. This secret is up to the DM and might take the form of a supernatural gift |

# Bejeweled Conclave Characters

Joining the Bejeweled Conclave is advantageous for any character with mysterious allure, regardless of whether they use magic to enchant others. Those skilled at uncovering and trading secrets are also well suited to this faction, as are entertainers who specialize in dancing, singing, or other performance arts.

The most sought-after recruits are Bards, Rogues, Sorcerers, Warlocks, or Wizards (especially those with the Enchanter subclass). Characters with proficiency in Deception, Performance, Persuasion, or Sleight of Hand or who have the Bejeweled Conclave Spy, Entertainer, or Noble background are also likely to be recruited.

**Member Benefits**  
If you're a member of the Bejeweled Conclave, you receive these benefits.

**Finer Things.** The conclave ensures its members dress well, paying you a stipend that supports your Wealthy lifestyle (4 GP per day).

**Trinket.** Roll on the Bejeweled Conclave Trinkets table to determine what trinket you have from your time with the Bejeweled Conclave.

**Bejeweled Conclave Trinkets**

| 1d6 | Trinket |
|---|---|
| 1 | An empty perfume bottle that smells faintly of longing |
| 2 | Three love letters in the same handwriting, signed with different names |
| 3 | A silk scarf with several hidden pockets |
| 4 | The signature page from a contract |
| 5 | A drinking glass carved with a comet |
| 6 | A gaudy engagement ring with a fake gem |

# Using This Faction

As well-connected spies and secret keepers, members of the Bejeweled Conclave can provide characters with useful information. For example, the conclave might help the characters if they've lost a lead or are having trouble gaining access to an important public figure. The conclave might insist on a favor or secret in return, pulling the characters into its webs of intrigue.

# Special Facility

Members of the Bejeweled Conclave can add the following special facility to their Bastions.

## Entertainment Salon

*Level 5 Bastion Facility*

**Prerequisite:** Membership in the Bejeweled Conclave

**Space:** Roomy

**Hirelings:** 2

**Order:** Research

This fancy salon boasts elegant wall hangings, comfortable reclining couches, and a well-stocked bar.

**Open Pockets.** Your eloquent hirelings convince others to pay a little more or to accept a little less. When you roll a die to determine how many Gold Pieces you pay or gain for a Bastion order or event, you can roll twice and take either result.

**Research: Learn Secrets.** When you issue the Research order to this facility, you direct the facility's hirelings to entertain well-informed contacts and learn about a specific creature you name within 50 miles of your Bastion. After 7 days of work, the hirelings gain 1d4 facts about the named creature that aren't widely known and might be amusing, embarrassing, or useful. The hirelings also discover the creature's power relative to yours (such as whether the creature's CR is higher than, lower than, or the same as your level). At the DM's discretion, you might receive limited or incorrect information about an exceptionally private or supernaturally disguised creature.

name: Bringers of the Cosmic Dawn
description:
A secretive organization of amoral transmuters, the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn receives abstruse directives from alien entities that hail from the dark spaces between stars. Faction members magically mutate plants and creatures in preparation for visitation by these beings—an event they believe is inevitable. They believe these entities will witness their glorious transmutations, be impressed, and bring about an exalted future full of mutated aberrations that serve transmuters' every whim.

# Goals and Activities

The exact goals of the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn are inscrutable to many members, though all believe they are helping to usher an ascended age of existence. The faction draws unprincipled transmuters, fringe scientists, and irrational astronomers to its academy and observatory, the Cosmic Oculus, where they receive fractured instructions from the faction's five leaders, known as the Starspeakers.

These communications have a consistent message: Faction members must transmute the flora and fauna surrounding the Cosmic Oculus. Invariably, this involves transforming plants into hostile, flesh-eating specimens and mutating beasts to rearrange organs, add joints to limbs, and cause them to secrete slime. In doing so, the faction hopes to gain the attention of alien entities they believe will descend and warp all worlds in their path.

The faction members are united in purpose but not in execution. Some pursue their own theories of mutation and transfiguration, experimenting on themselves as much as on other subjects. Some instructions communicated by the Starspeakers conflict with others, as though the alien entities they seek to communicate with weren't working in concert. These contradictions mean that the faction's work advances erratically, with rejected experiments as common as transformations deemed to be in concordance with the aliens' will.

**Dawnrise Canyon**  
Bringers of Cosmic Dawn members carry out most transmutations far from public scrutiny. The faction is based in the secluded Dawnrise Canyon, far below the clifftop where the Cosmic Oculus stands. The once-tranquil canyon is now a dangerous valley of frightening creatures, hostile plants, aggressive transmuters, and wandering aberrations drawn to the unnatural landscape. Time moves erratically in the region thanks to frequent use of time-altering magic to speed up or slow down specific mutations.

**Opposition to the Far Realm**  
While outsiders might not comprehend the distinction between the alien intelligences the Starspeakers commune with and the monsters of the Far Realm, Bringers of Cosmic Dawn members fear and reject the Far Realm as unknowable, indescribable, and inimical to life. The faction works to counter Far Realm incursions and expels any members who deal directly with that domain of incomprehensible horror.

# Leadership and Organization

The Bringers of the Cosmic Dawn lacks a rigid hierarchy, but its leaders maintain careful control over the information they receive from both members' experiments and alien intelligences.

**Member Roles**  
Certain members of the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn have special roles in the faction.

**Starspeakers.** The five enigmatic Starspeakers command the entire faction. None answer to any name besides their title, and they rarely leave the Cosmic Oculus except to measure progress within Dawnrise Canyon. Four Starspeakers (Medium Aberrant Cultists) are human. The fifth and most senior Starspeaker appears to be an elderly human astronomer, but she is actually a magically disguised Aboleth who has eschewed the Far Realm.

**Worldwarpers.** Most faction members work at the Cosmic Oculus or Dawnrise Canyon, but others, called Worldwarpers, venture into civilized lands to engage in more far-flung experimentation. Worldwarpers seek out willing recipients to, as they put it, "gain blessings from beyond the stars."

Worldwarpers might offer to improve a banker's garden with voracious plants to deter thieves, provide an aberration to help guard a prison, or augment a diplomat's body to produce intoxicating pheromones. Like the work in Dawnrise Canyon, these puzzling changes ostensibly further a wider agenda, but Worldwarpers are rarely aware of the end goals; they merely put pieces in place as commanded and report back to the Starspeakers.

**Blots.** The Starspeakers secretly assign faction members to find and eradicate Far Realm sympathizers. These individuals, known within the faction as Blots, also venture into places where the Far Realm's stain bleeds into the world, seeking to quash the Far Realm's presence wherever they find it.

## Things Beyond the Stars

The Bringers of Cosmic Dawn receives messages from many alien intelligences, not all of which are aligned with one another. You can use the Alien Entities table to generate sample intelligences that are directing the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn.

**Alien Entities**

| 1d6 | Entity |
|---|---|
| 1 | Atropus, the World Born Dead, is a malevolent entity the size of a planetoid that drifts ever closer to the world. |
| 2 | Dendar, the Night Serpent, is a colossal beast that feeds on nightmares generated by its warped mind. |
| 3 | Tharizdun, the Chained God, is a dark spiral of roiling nothingness. It seeks freedom from its millennia-long imprisonment and the extinction of all life. |
| 4 | Xhalovix is an amalgamation of 9,999 mutated planets preparing to ascend to godhood once it has transformed its ten-thousandth world. |
| 5 | Trapped beneath a ruined city, Zargon the Returner seeks loyal worshippers to restore his mutation-steeped realm of slime and decadence. The dark sky reveals his malign will to those who know how to interpret it. |
| 6 | Ejected from the Negative Plane, a nameless evil entity drives mortals to despair by twisting reality into impossible forms. |

## Joining the Bringers

Transmuters might seek out the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn even if they don't wish to advance the faction's goals. Faction members are undeniable masters of Transmutation magic, and some daring characters might join long enough to learn their secrets. Although some transmuters escape the faction, far too many begin to believe the Starspeakers' ramblings and become devotees—or worse, they become unwilling subjects for experimental mutations when their disloyalty is uncovered.

## Cosmic Oculus

Once an abandoned observatory, the Cosmic Oculus became the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn's base when the faction discovered that the facility seems to magically amplify the messages of entities between the stars. In addition to the Starspeakers, faction astronomers also live in the Cosmic Oculus to record psychic signals from deep space and make nightly measurements of celestial bodies.

Most faction members never see the inside of the Cosmic Oculus. The ramshackle buildings clustered along the cliff face between the observatory and the canyon have expanded and mutated on their own, and members have used spells such as Stone Shape and Fabricate to haphazardly extend walls, enclose laboratories, and create passageways through the rock.

# Renown Rewards

Characters gain renown with the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn by engaging in aberrant transmutations or completing faction quests to recover rare ritual ingredients, samples of unusual flora and fauna, or astronomical measurements from distant locations. As their Renown Scores increase, characters gain access to various perks, as shown on the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn Renown table. If your campaign doesn't use renown, the DM decides if and when characters earn these perks.

**Bringers of the Cosmic Dawn Renown**

| Renown Score | Reward |
|---|---|
| 3+ | You can freely enter Dawnrise Canyon, though you are afforded no specific protections from its dangers. |
| 5+ | The Bringers of Cosmic Dawn warns you when you travel near places with Far Realm influence or a significant number of Aberrations. |
| 10 | The first time your Renown Score reaches 10, the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn gives you an Uncommon magic item from the Scroll, Potion, or Wondrous Item category. |
| 15+ | 1d4 Cultists, convinced you embody a prophecy, become your loyal followers. You can order this retinue to assist you for one mission. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases. |
| 20+ | You can buy Common and Uncommon Spell Scrolls that contain Transmutation spells from faction members. |
| 25+ | 1d4 Cultist Fanatics join your retinue of loyal followers. |
| 30+ | The first time your Renown Score reaches 30, the faction teaches you its transmuting magic. You always have the Alter Self spell prepared, and you can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a Long Rest. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell (choose when you gain this reward). You can also cast this spell using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level. |
| 40+ | You can buy Rare Spell Scrolls that contain Transmutation spells from faction members. |
| 50+ | Faction members openly share information with you. Additionally, the first time your Renown score reaches 50, you can undertake voluntary mutations to enhance your physiology. You have Advantage on saving throws made to avoid or end the Grappled and Poisoned conditions. |

# Bringers of Cosmic Dawn Characters

Most members of the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn are transmutation-focused mages, but any characters with an interest in astronomy, aberrations, or warping life are welcome. New recruits aren't permitted to balk at the faction's creations or goals.

The most welcome recruits are Sorcerers (especially those with the Aberrant Sorcery subclass), Warlocks (especially those with the Great Old One Patron subclass), or Wizards (especially those with the Transmuter subclass). Characters with proficiency in Arcana, Medicine, or Nature or with Navigator's Tools are also valued as recruits, as are characters with the Cosmic Dawn Experiment, Guide, or Hermit background.

**Member Benefits**  
If you're a member of the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn, you receive these benefits.

**Starwatcher Gear.** The Bringers of Cosmic Dawn provide you with Navigator's Tools and a blank notebook in which to record your astronomical observations.

**Trinket.** Roll on the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn Trinkets table to determine what trinket you have from your time with the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn.

**Bringers of Cosmic Dawn Trinkets**

| 1d6 | Trinket |
|---|---|
| 1 | A razor-sharp, violet-tinted talon |
| 2 | An uneven spyglass lens that casts flickering pale-green light |
| 3 | A stone carved with stars in an unfamiliar constellation |
| 4 | Fragments of a prophecy about flumphs |
| 5 | A fern frond that twitches like a tentacle |
| 6 | A small box containing a worm that won't die |

# Using This Faction

The Bringers of Cosmic Dawn can easily serve as a villainous or amoral organization in your campaign. If the characters pursue villains to the Celestial Oculus, you can determine whether the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn fight the characters with the aid of powerful Transmutation magic and strange Aberrations, or if they turn out to be curious intellectuals duped by malign influences.

However, the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn need not be villains. The characters might need the faction's extensive knowledge of Transmutation magic to undo a shape-shifting curse or restore a transmuted ally to the proper form. Members' whispers about creatures from the depths of space might presage an incursion by conquering githyanki astride dragons or a fleet of mind flayers on spelljamming vessels.

# Special Facility

Members of the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn can add the following special facility to their Bastions.

## Transmutation Vat

*Level 5 Bastion Facility*

**Prerequisite:** Membership in the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn

**Space:** Cramped

**Hirelings:** 1

**Order:** Harvest

This laboratory features a vat or cauldron simmering with transformation potential.

**Harvest:** Fluid Transmutation. When you issue the Harvest order to this facility, you instruct your hireling to pour a substance into the vat and transform it into something else. You must expend a Common or Uncommon potion, which is destroyed in the vat. At the end of 7 days, the hireling produces your choice of a flask of Alchemist's Fire, a vial of Antitoxin, a vial of Basic Poison, or a Common or Uncommon potion of your choice.

**Enlarging the Facility.** You can enlarge your Transmutation Vat into a Roomy facility by spending 2,000 GP. When you issue the Harvest order to a Roomy Transmutation Vat, you can expend two Common or Uncommon potions. If you do, your hireling produces two substances of your choice instead of one; the options can be different.

name: Covenant of the Grave
description:
The Covenant of the Grave is a loose affiliation of necromancers and those interested in studying death and undeath through a disciplined, scientific lens. The covenant has no room for megalomaniacs who seek domination via hordes of undead minions.

These realists are aware that their studies, no matter how clinical, unnerve most people, so their members are unobtrusive and their laboratories hidden. The greatest covenant academy is the Pale Tower, a morbid, bone-white structure far from civilization.

# Goals and Activities

Covenant members are typically more interested in deepening their knowledge than their power. They freely share their research with each other via correspondence, personal visits, or clandestine lectures, but they rarely reveal discoveries to those outside the organization. Many worry that their research might be misused for sinister, nonacademic ends. Others simply don't expect anyone but like-minded scholars to comprehend their work.

Unlike necromancers who incite undead uprisings, the Covenant of the Grave usually works to stymie undead hordes and return less powerful undead to the safer confines of the laboratory or grave. Members consider undead rampages dreadfully unscientific, if not outright embarrassing. They're keenly aware of the harm that such villainous necromancy brings to the faction's reputation. Their opposition to necromantic wickedness sometimes puts the faction in conflict with powerful undead such as liches, death knights, or vampires.

# Leadership and Organization

Although an established hierarchy exists within the Covenant of the Grave, members are usually too engrossed in their own research to worry about rank.

## Necrodemics and Gravetenders

Any faction member who shares a significant scholarly truth about death, decay, or undeath with the faction might gain the title of Necrodemic. Some members hold expanded titles such as Arisen Necrodemic or Necrodemic Embalmist, awarded for sharing more complex knowledge.

The title of Gravetender is held by the three head administrators of the Pale Tower. Emeritus administrators keep this title after retirement, so four to six Gravetenders usually exist at a time. Gravetenders set the overall direction for the faction but are usually bookish and circumspect, so change within the faction is gradual.

## Joining the Covenant

Any spellcaster with an interest in Necromancy magic or macabre research is likely to hear about the Covenant of the Grave, but the faction doesn't actively recruit. The covenant expects aspirants to independently identify its members and present a well-reasoned proposal for membership. A member who receives a qualified aspirant usually confers with other members before either taking on the aspirant as a research assistant or sending them to study at the Pale Tower.

## Undead Members

Only a few members of the Covenant of the Grave are undead. Covenant members have little use for less powerful undead such as skeletons and zombies, and other undead are usually too consumed by their hungers to maintain the intellectual rigor the covenant expects. The Undead Members table details the few undead scholars in the covenant.

**Undead Members**

| Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Adlin Humbington | A bookish Ghost who haunts his surgical theater, Adlin is so tied to his experiments that he's unaware he's dead. |
| Kadra Faldrig | The Lawful Neutral Lich Kadra hides that she's undead so her highly regarded insights into lichdom seem inspired by intellect rather than a study of her own nature. |
| Melodin the Risen | A determined Revenant, Melodin is a Gravetender of the Pale Tower who seeks to avenge herself against her predecessor by proving herself the superior administrator. |

## The Pale Tower

The greatest concentration of covenant members resides in the Pale Tower. Rising from a noxious swamp, this bone-white structure is thousands of years old. The tower's small, dingy exterior belies its underground warren of classrooms, laboratories, and ossuaries.

In addition to being an academy and research institution, the Pale Tower is a repository of sinister necromantic magic that the covenant doesn't want misused. Rumors hold that malicious artifacts, lost Necromancy spells, and soul-staining magic items are locked away in vaults only the Gravetenders can access.

# Renown Rewards

Characters gain renown with the Covenant of the Grave by sharing scholarly insights into death or undeath or by completing quests for the Covenant. As their Renown Scores increase, characters gain access to various perks, as shown on the Covenant of the Grave Renown table. If your campaign doesn't use renown, the DM decides if and when characters earn these perks.

**Covenant of the Grave Renown**

| Renown Score | Reward |
|---|---|
| 3+ | You receive free lodging at the Pale Tower and can access its extensive subterranean libraries. The covenant safely contains or destroys malevolent magic items you surrender to its care. |
| 5+ | You can purchase the costly Material components required for Necromancy spells you can cast from covenant members. |
| 10 | The first time your Renown Score reaches 10, the covenant gives you an Uncommon magic item from the Rod or Wand category. |
| 15+ | Covenant members freely cast the Remove Curse spell on you and your allies. |
| 20+ | You earn the honorary title of Necrodemic. When you surrender a magic item to the covenant, the covenant gifts you a different magic item of an equal or lesser rarity from the same category as the surrendered item. |
| 25+ | You can arrange for a meeting with any of the faction's Gravetenders. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases. |
| 30 | The first time your Renown Score reaches 30, the faction shares necromantic secrets with you. You always have the Speak with Dead spell prepared, and you can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a Long Rest. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell (choose when you gain this reward). You can also cast this spell using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level. |
| 40 | You earn the honorary title of Arisen Necrodemic. You can request the help of 1d4 Mages for one mission. Once you use this reward, you can't do so again until your Renown Score increases. |
| 50+ | If you or one of your allies dies and the body is brought to the Pale Tower, a covenant member casts a Resurrection spell, targeting the deceased. This reward is free the first time you use it. On subsequent occasions, you must provide any Material components normally consumed by the spell. |

# Covenant of the Grave Characters

Joining the Covenant of the Grave is advantageous to any character interested in the secrets of life and death. While intellectual rigor is important, knowledge of any death-adjacent subject is sufficient for aspiring members.

The most welcome aspirants are Clerics, Monks, and Wizards (especially those with the Necromancer subclass). Characters with proficiency in Arcana, Investigation, or Medicine; proficiency with Leatherworker's Tools; or the Covenant of the Grave Recruit, Sage, or Scribe background are also good fits.

## Member Benefits

If you're a member of the Covenant of the Grave, you receive these benefits.

**Grave Services.** The covenant respectfully performs final rites for your corpse whenever the inevitable comes to pass.

**Modest Lifestyle.** The covenant pays you a stipend that supports your Modest lifestyle (1 GP per day).

**Trinket.** Roll on the Covenant of the Grave Trinkets table to determine what trinket you have from your time with the covenant.

**Covenant of the Grave Trinkets**

| 1d6 | Trinket |
|---|---|
| 1 | A tin of grave dirt |
| 2 | A self-sterilizing trephine |
| 3 | A chapbook with illustrations of graveyards |
| 4 | A zombie's twitching toe |
| 5 | A small wreath of dried flowers in an old box |
| 6 | A mysterious organ in a jar of amber fluid |

# Using This Faction

Faction members might warn the characters of potential necromantic uprisings or escort the party through lands plagued with undead. Having access to graveyards and burial houses, the faction might also recover the corpse of someone the characters want to revive or question.

The covenant isn't likely to aid the characters for free. Members might request lost necromantic lore in exchange for their help or task the party with defeating a necromancer or undead creature who has rejected the covenant's academic overtures.

# Special Facility

Members of the Covenant of the Grave can add the following special facility to their Bastions.

## Morgue

*Level 5 Bastion Facility*

**Prerequisite:** Membership in the Covenant of the Grave

**Space:** Cramped

**Hirelings:** 1

**Order:** Research

A morgue is a location where corpses are stored and studied. You can store up to four Small or Medium corpses in the Morgue.

**Corpse Storage.** As long as this facility's hireling is present, each corpse stored in the Morgue is affected by the Gentle Repose spell. If the facility lacks a hireling or a corpse is removed, the facility's corpses or the removed corpse loses this protection until returned to a Morgue with a hireling.
